text.p: A five-nation monitoring group including the United States said on Friday Israel was responsible for shelling a south Lebanese village last week and "deplored" the damage and injuries it caused.
It called the shelling a "tragedy" and urged measures to prevent any repetition.

In its first public statement since its formation, the group said Israeli forces were responsible "for the manner in which they carried out, against a Lebanese armed group, counterfire which resulted in the damage and injuries at Safad el-Battikh."

"The Monitoring Group urges that appropriate measures be taken by responsible authorities to ensure that such tragedies will not be repeated," the statement issued in Beirut by the Lebanese Foreign Ministry said.
It said the shelling injured 13 civilians, four seriously, and damaged four houses and the village's electrical grid, telephone lines and water distribution network.

An Israeli army statement said the committee "expressed deep regret at the fact that civilians were wounded but did not place direct responsibility for the incident on Israel and refrained from condemning Israel or determining that Israel violated the understandings as the Syrian and Lebanese delegations suggested."

The monitoring group stopped short of saying whether the shelling breached a U.S.-sponsored April 26 ceasefire understanding in south Lebanon that banned all attacks from or against civilian areas by Israeli troops and the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas who are fighting them.
It said the damage and casualties were the result of Israeli counterfire after a Hizbollah mortar attack. It avoided the key issue of whether the mortars were fired from the shelled village.
If they were, Israel could argue that its shelling of the village was justified under a clause in the April 26 understanding that grants both sides the right to self-defence.
"Concluding its discussions, the Monitoring Group deplored the injuries caused to the Lebanese civilians in the village of Safad el-Battikh," the statement said.

The monitoring group, which includes representatives of the United States, France, Syria, Lebanon and Israel, issued the statement after a marathon five-day meeting in south Lebanon to discuss a Lebanese complaint about the shelling.

The complaint was the third Lebanon has lodged since the monitoring group began operating but the group has never before issued a public statement. It followed Lebanese press reports that its discussions were deadlocked.
The group was set up under the April 26 understanding to monitor observance of the ceasefire which ended a 17-day Israeli blitz of Lebanon intended to destroy Hizbollah.

The understanding was designed to end Israeli shelling of civilian areas in south Lebanon and Hizbollah Katyusha salvoes against north Israel and to provide a mechanism to prevent escalation when attacks occurred.
Israel first said last weekend that it shelled Safad el-Battikh in retaliation after guerrillas fired mortars from the village at its troops.

However, the statement said Israel's representative expressed sorrow to the group for the injuries and damage caused and said they were an "unintended" result of defensive countermeasures after a Hizbollah attack.
The Lebanese and Syrian representatives said the shelling of the village was deliberate, the statement said.

"The Lebanese and Syrian representatives expressed the view that the shelling was deliberate and voiced the concern that the Israeli artillery action was aimed at raising tension to prepare the ground for a wider Israeli military action," it added.
The Israeli representative denied this, it said.

"During the committee's discussions, it was stated that Israel's reaction was restrained and that the army fired a small number of shells which were aimed at the source of the Hizbollah fire," the Israeli army statement said.
